sentences.text: Mirischia was a small bipedal predator that lived in northeastern Brazil during the Early Cretaceous.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a partial articulated skeleton with the pelvis, incomplete hind limbs, vertebrae, ribs, and thigh bones.
All skeletal elements of this animal exhibit an exceptionally thin bone wall.
A piece of petrified intestine was preserved in front of the pubic bones of the holotype.
The specimen preserves soft tissue remains, including a hollow space interpreted as an air sac between the pubic and ischial bones.
The specific name asymmetrica refers to the asymmetry between the left and right ischium in the fossil specimen.
The ischia of Mirischia are asymmetrical, with the left bone having an oval hole and the right bone having an open notch.
Estimates of its size vary, with a 2004 length of 2.1 meters and a 2010 weight estimate of seven kilograms.
The species Mirischia asymmetrica was named and described in 2004 by David Martill, Eberhard Frey, and Darren Naish.
In 2004, Mirischia was classified within the Compsognathidae family.
In 2010, Darren Naish suggested that Mirischia might be a basal member of the Tyrannosauroidea.
A 2024 study by Andrea Cau placed Mirischia in a polytomy within basal Coelurosauria, excluding it from the Compsognathus genus.
